title: Amendment 3
short: Abortion limits & minors' gender transition care
yes_does: Repeals the 2024 reproductive-freedom amendment. Allows abortion only for medical emergencies, fetal anomalies, and rape or incest up to 12 weeks; requires parental consent for minors; bans gender transition procedures for minors.
no_does: Keeps the 2024 amendment voters passed, which protects abortion access up to fetal viability. No new constitutional ban on minors' transition care.
note: The 2024 abortion-rights amendment passed with 51.6%. Polls show this one deadlocked.

title: Amendment 6
yes_does: Makes initiative and referendum a fundamental right. Lawmakers could only change a voter-passed law with 80% of both chambers plus a statewide vote. Courts could rewrite unfair ballot summaries. Keeps today's signature and simple-majority rules.
no_does: No change: the legislature can still amend or repeal laws that voters pass by initiative.
note: Nearly a third of voters were unsure in August.

title: Amendment 7
short: “Show-Me Prosperity Fund” to eventually end state taxes
yes_does: Creates a permanent state endowment invested in index funds. Nothing can be spent until the Treasurer certifies its earnings can replace state taxes; then those taxes are eliminated and can't be brought back except in a shortfall.
no_does: No endowment fund; state taxes stay as they are.
note: Where the fund's starting money comes from isn't spelled out.

title: Amendment 8
yes_does: Puts the 4-year election of county sheriffs and their duties into the constitution. An elected sheriff could only be removed by a quo warranto case brought by the Attorney General. St. Louis, St. Louis County and St. Charles County are exempt.
no_does: Sheriff elections, duties and removal stay in regular state law, which the legislature can change.

title: Proposition A
yes_does: Approves the 2025 map (House Bill 1), which would likely shift Missouri's U.S. House delegation from 6–2 to 7–1 Republican in future elections.
no_does: Rejects the 2025 map and keeps the 2022 district lines.
note: On Sept 25 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled the 2022 map is used for this November's House races either way.

title: State Auditor
short: Only statewide office on the ballot
yes_does: Quentin Wilson (D) is a former director of the Missouri Department of Revenue. Libertarian Dustin Coffell is also running.
no_does: Scott Fitzpatrick (R) is the incumbent, seeking a second term.
note: SLU's poll is the only public one; its margin of error on this question is ±5.9.
